To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the likelihood ratio for an exponential model is more powerful than those of normal parametric models and normal and exponential kernel estimators, when data are exponentially distributed.

the biweight kernel is the most effective kernel for the analysis of data from the exponentially distributed model and the biweight kernel with the boundary adaptation is the most effective of all the kernels considered for data from the exponentially or the normally distributed model.

the likelihood ratio based on the biweight kernel is more likely than the likelihood ratios based on the other methods to support a correct inference that two groups are from the same population and less likely to support the incorrect inference that two groups from the same population are from different populations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an improved method of determining likelihood ratios for the two-level model in forensic science.
the use of likelihood ratio procedures in forensic science, and in particular, the evaluation of evidence for data that are exponentially distributed.
the use of kernel estimation to determine likelihood ratios for the evaluation of evidence for a two-level random-effects model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biweight kernel with adaptation at the boundary provides the most accurate and reliable likelihood ratios for exponentially distributed data, and is the best kernel to use in this situation.
, in the context of the present study, the biweight kernel is a good choice for a two-level exponential model, but that it would be unwise to rely on a parametric model in this context.
the biweight kernel with adaptation at the boundary provides an excellent performance, with the normal kernel providing a good second-best performance and that the parametric models perform poorly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biweight kernel is superior to the normal kernel and to the normal model.
the biweight kernel with boundary adaptation gives a good performance for the exponential model and is a good alternative to the use of parametric models.

, when there are a small number of fragments in each set and the between-group distribution of the data may be thought to be very positively skewed, a biweight kernel is a useful alternative to the normal kernel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biweight kernel is a very useful kernel for the analysis of data from two-level models when the between-group data is very skewed.
, when the between-group data is positively skewed, the biweight kernel is a better choice than the normal kernel.

, in the case of the aluminium data, the likelihood ratio based on the biweight kernel with adaptation is more supportive of the propositions that the groups are from different sources and that the groups are the same source than the likelihood ratios based on the normal kernel estimation procedure and parametric models.
